title: Probing intermittent polariton vortex dynamics with two-point correlations
authors: R. Cherbunin, A. Liubomirov, P. Kozhevin, M. Chukeev, M. Petrov, S. Kavokina, A. Nalitov, A. Kavokin
abstract: Superconducting single-photon detectors with time resolution of 80 ps have been used to study the spatiotemporal dynamics of a trapped bosonic condensate of exciton-polaritons. Both second- and first-order correlation functions are found to exhibit pronounced oscillations in time governed by the dynamics of the polariton condensate in the trap. We have identified the intermittent regime of stochastic transitions between stationary and limit-cycle regimes near the Andronov-Hopf bifurcation manifested in asymmetric distortions of the correlation function. This rich interplay of deterministic and stochastic condensate dynamics is explained theoretically as a manifestation of mutually compensating self-repulsion and reservoir-mediated attraction.
summary: The paper uses two-point correlation measurements on exciton-polariton condensates to probe their vortex dynamics. It reveals an intermittent regime where the system stochastically switches between stable and oscillating states near a critical bifurcation point. This rich quantum fluid behavior is theoretically explained by balancing nonlinear self-repulsion against reservoir-mediated attraction.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex, intermittent dynamics of polariton vortices within a trapped bosonic condensate.
main_result: The research identifies an intermittent regime characterized by stochastic transitions between stationary and limit-cycle dynamics near an Andronov-Hopf bifurcation. This behavior is explained by the interplay between self-repulsion and reservoir-mediated attraction.
method: Measurements involve using superconducting single-photon detectors to probe two-point second-order correlation functions, $g^{(2)}(	au)$, which are theoretically modeled using an extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE).
model_or_system: The system is a trapped bosonic condensate of exciton-polaritons in a microcavity. The dynamics are described by the eGPE, which models pseudospin precession and exhibits rich nonlinear behavior near bifurcations.
key_observables: Two-point second-order correlation function $g^{(2)}(	au)$, oscillations in $g^{(2)}$ frequency, and asymmetry in $g^{(2)}$ at low pump power.
important_parameters: Pump power (fluctuating across the Andronov-Hopf bifurcation threshold), trap ellipticity, and parameters governing self-repulsion ($\xi$) and attraction ($\epsilon$).
main_assumptions: The analysis requires an extended Gross-Pitaevskii model beyond the adiabatic approximation to correctly analyze stability near bifurcations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the intermittent dynamics near a bifurcation, show $g^{(2)}$ measurements for various configurations across different pump power regimes, and depict limit cycles on the Bloch sphere related to the AH bifurcation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the measurement technique using $g^{(2)}$, then theoretically modeling the system with eGPE, identifying the transition points (AH bifurcation), and finally demonstrating how fluctuations induce stochastic switching between stable and oscillatory states in the correlation function.
why_interesting: This work connects concepts from nonlinear dynamics (bifurcations, intermittency) directly to quantum optics phenomena in polariton condensates, providing a detailed mechanism for observing complex time-dependent behavior beyond simple mean-field descriptions.
